proof_summary: At \(n=602191\), the intermediate odd number \(k=a(n)+4=6735401372843\) lies strictly between the two proposed consecutive values. The residue classes \(m\equiv0\pmod2,\ 3\pmod4,\ 1\pmod3,\ 1\pmod8,\ 13\pmod{16},\ 21\pmod{48},\ 5\pmod{48}\) cover every positive exponent, and modular computation shows that in these cases \(k2^m+1\) is divisible respectively by \(3,5,7,17,257,97,673\), so \(k\) is itself a Sierpiński number.
